This article is the reviewer-facing entry point for the JSS submission version
of **gamlss.longitudinal**. It connects the paper, package interface,
diagnostics, examples, and replication workflow.

## What the package does

`gamlss.longitudinal` fits longitudinal GAMLSS models with first-order copula
dependence between adjacent repeated measurements. The main interface is
`gamlss_longitudinal()`. Each supported marginal parameter and copula parameter
can have its own formula, including fixed and smooth covariate effects.

The package is intended for analyses where the marginal distributional shape or
within-subject dependence is part of the scientific question. It is not an
automatic imputation tool, an arbitrary higher-order vine fitting package, or a
time-series forecasting engine beyond prediction on supplied new panels.

## Quick install check

After installing the package, run the smoke test:

```{r smoke-test, eval=TRUE}
source(system.file("smoke-tests", "new-user-smoke.R",
  package = "gamlss.longitudinal"
))
```

## Recommended workflow

The main user workflow is:

1. Inspect the longitudinal response and missingness pattern.
2. Screen candidate marginal distributions.
3. Screen candidate copula families.
4. Fit the longitudinal GAMLSS-copula model.
5. Inspect convergence, coefficients, and uncertainty.
6. Check marginal and dependence diagnostics.
7. Predict distributional summaries or simulate from the fitted model.

The minimal workflow article demonstrates this path:

```{r minimal-workflow}
vignette("standard-workflow", package = "gamlss.longitudinal")
```

For a longer known-truth example, use:

```{r detailed-workflow}
vignette("native-simulation-workflow", package = "gamlss.longitudinal")
```

## Main interface

A typical model fit has separate formulas for marginal and dependence
parameters:

```{r fit-template}
fit <- gamlss_longitudinal(
  mu.formula = response ~ time + group + s(baseline),
  sigma.formula = ~ time + group,
  theta.formula = ~ time + group,
  data = dat,
  time_var = "time",
  subject_var = "id",
  margin_dist = GA(),
  copula_dist = "N",
  optimization = "joint"
)
summary(fit)
```

The default `optimization = "joint"` updates marginal parameters against the
joint margin-copula objective. For an explicit RS sensitivity fit that excludes
the copula contribution from marginal updates, request
`optimization = "separate"`. Optimizer tuning is grouped in one
validated control object rather than spread across the fit call:

Separate optimization does not generally maximize the joint likelihood.
Consequently, its reported joint log likelihood, AIC, and BIC are descriptive
values at the separate estimates; do not use them for a standard likelihood-
ratio comparison with a joint fit. Use joint optimization for final
likelihood-based comparisons.

```{r optimizer-controls, eval=FALSE}
control <- gamlss_longitudinal_control(
  outer_tol = 1e-4,
  max_outer_iter = 100,
  rs = list(inner_tol = 1e-5, max_inner_iter = 50)
)
fit <- gamlss_longitudinal(
  data = dat,
  margin_dist = GA(),
  copula_dist = "t",
  time_var = "time",
  subject_var = "id",
  optimization = "joint",
  optimizer_control = control
)
```

Use the final JSS paper example for the exact family, copula, and covariates.

The ordered unique values of `time_var` define scheduled adjacency. Numeric
spacing is not treated as elapsed-time distance, factor-level order defines the
schedule for factors, and pair-level copula covariates are evaluated at the
earlier scheduled row. Model elapsed-time effects explicitly when required.

## Standard methods to inspect

Reviewers should be able to inspect fitted objects through standard R methods:

```{r standard-methods}
coef(fit)
vcov(fit)
confint(fit)
logLik(fit)
nobs(fit)
formula(fit)
terms(fit)
fitted(fit)
residuals(fit)
model.frame(fit)
```

Prediction and simulation use standard generics:

```{r predict-simulate}
predict(fit, newdata = newdat, type = "mean")
simulate(fit, nsim = 10)
```

## Diagnostics

Marginal and dependence diagnostics should both be reviewed for this model
class. Fit-time warnings report objective conditions such as non-convergence or
unavailable covariance; `check_model()` is an optional descriptive numerical
report rather than a prerequisite:

```{r diagnostics}
plot(fit)
plot_terms(fit)
plot_margin_fit(fit)
plot_copula_diagnostics(fit)
plot_copula_diagnostics(fit, type = "all", ncol = 3)
check_model(fit)
check_missingness(
  dat,
  response_var = "response",
  subject_var = "id",
  time_var = "time"
)
```

See the diagnostics guide for interpretation:

```{r diagnostics-vignette}
vignette("diagnostics-decisions", package = "gamlss.longitudinal")
```


## Paper replication

Paper replication lives in the separate
[paper repository](https://github.com/ahibbert/working-paper-gamlss-long). Follow its
[reviewer guide](https://github.com/ahibbert/working-paper-gamlss-long/blob/main/paper/REVIEWER.md), currently a
release-preparation draft at its intended publication location. Use the exact
software/paper source pair named in the release record and assemble a fresh
workspace from those clones or archives before running the paper commands.
The prepared guide and source pair are not yet a verified public release.

The paper `smoke` profile checks a small synthetic workflow. The `paper`
profile rebuilds assets from versioned analysis-ready inputs and refits the
declared ACTG analyses; `full` recomputes the declared studies and application
analyses. Both retain the historical ACTG selection ledgers. They are separate
from package tests and the installed new-user smoke test.

Use the companion guide for exact commands, external output directories,
resource requirements and current run records. Run paper commands from the
assembled workspace, not this package checkout. A passing package test does
not establish end-to-end reproduction of the paper.
